rationale: The candidate reads as a highly fragmented, starburst-like object with many overlapping facets and no stable dominant hall. Across views, the mass is coherent only as a blob of triangulated surfaces; it does not establish one clear long-span body, subordinate support bar, or daylight roof logic for a gymnasium. The top view is especially problematic: it collapses into a thin horizontal strip that contradicts the larger isometric/front silhouette, suggesting view-to-view inconsistency rather than one spatial rule. There is also no legible public void, court, entry seam, or undercut on the access edge, so the blue frontage is not meaningfully addressed. Because the form behaves more like a faceted sculptural aggregation than a usable gym hall, it fails the program hard gate.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is far more fragmented and rotational than this calm linear hall; do not imitate the envelope, only the notion of a dominant hall with a subordinate edge.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A long, low sports datum with a light roof and clear edge condition can support a gymmatic public program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate lacks the single-hall readability and grounded entry sequence seen here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A legible long-span volume with strong roof expression and a clear public frontage fits the gymnasium brief.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate has almost no coherent void; this is the opposite spatial principle.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A carved court/void and deep covered threshold can create strong public ground for sports use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Useful only as a void-and-canopy precedent; the candidate is not yet organized around a legible court.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Threshold + roof-over-void can make a sports building feel civic and active at ground.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like aggregation can work for sports facilities when subvolumes stay subordinate to the main use.
